briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Relief on the Ballot, Psilocybin Nears the Finish Line
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis market is proving more resilient than feared under the new 24% wholesale tax, and now has a real shot at rolling it back depending on who wins the governor's mansion in November. Nationally, rescheduling survived a court challenge and Compass Pathways' psilocybin program keeps racing toward what could be the first FDA-approved psychedelic medicine.

local.text: Michigan cannabis operators now have a political path out of the 24% wholesale tax: GOP gubernatorial nominee John James has vowed to kill the levy and is drawing cash and support from marijuana businesses as he heads into a November matchup with Jocelyn Benson, who has yet to stake out a position.

Despite the new tax, Michigan demand hasn't cracked: dispensaries moved 104,716 pounds of flower in February, up 3.2% year-over-year, with concentrates up 23.2% and vape carts up 18%, as licensed operators absorb costs in an oversupplied, hyper-competitive market rather than lose customers to the illicit trade.

The wholesale tax is also badly missing its own revenue targets — about $37 million in Q2 2026 against a projected $105 million per quarter — fueling the industry's argument in court (and at the ballot box) that the levy should be scrapped entirely.

Retail expansion keeps rolling in Washtenaw County: Lume Cannabis Co. opened a new Ann Arbor storefront on W. Liberty Street with an extended grand-opening weekend, adding to a market that already counts 18 active dispensaries in the city.

University of Michigan researchers just landed federal funding for a 12-month feasibility trial testing personalized marijuana coaching for adults with chronic lower back pain across 80 participants in Michigan and California — a sign mainstream medical research dollars are flowing back into cannabis.

national.text: Federal rescheduling cleared a major legal hurdle this week: the D.C. Circuit left the medical marijuana Schedule III reclassification in effect on Sept. 9, ruling that opponents hadn't shown grounds to block it, while the broader recreational rescheduling case awaits a DEA administrative law judge's recommendation.

The psychedelic medicine race just picked up speed: the FDA's new September 2026 framework is reshaping trial design and access rules for psilocybin and MDMA therapies, building on the agency's expedited-review commitments for lead candidates.

Compass Pathways remains the frontrunner for the first approved psychedelic drug, reporting 26-week Phase 3 results confirming COMP360's rapid onset and durable response in nearly 600 patients with treatment-resistant depression — data now feeding a rolling FDA submission under a priority review voucher.

M&A momentum keeps building: Vireo Growth is acquiring fellow MSO Planet 13 in an all-stock deal adding 36 dispensaries, part of a buying spree that will leave Vireo with roughly 265 stores across 15 states and cement it as one of the largest U.S. cannabis operators by store count.

The macro numbers back the optimism: state marijuana tax collections hit $986.8 million in Q2 2026, up about 11% year-over-year and nearly 16% over Q1, while a new industry survey found 73% of cannabis businesses expect federal rescheduling to meaningfully affect their operations.
